assessment:
Leave the live installation checks unchanged for this release. I found no small caching change that preserves their current behavior under concurrent file mutation.

The duplication is real: content() checks component evidence, then the aggregate recursively checks it again; verify() repeats installation validation for the aggregate and its children, and native workflow revisits both Skills. installation() reaches tooling_runtime.validate(), which hashes every support member.

A counterexample prevents straightforward memoization: validation succeeds, a support file changes, and a later claim requests the same installation. Today that later check refuses. A cached success would pass. Final revalidation detects persistent changes, but does not preserve every intermediate refusal opportunity. Metadata checks or advisory locks do not establish immutable inputs.

A future shared evaluation needs an enforced stable-input boundary: one evaluation context per check() invocation; separate identities for revision, manifest, installation reference, store/native root and runtime derivation; reuse only successful completed evaluations; fresh copies of returned installation data because installed_runtime() adds fields; distinct public-readback installations independently checked.

Memoizing bytes from an exact immutable Git commit is safe, but would not remove measured live-support hashing cost. Establishing runtime immutability now would add design and qualification work beyond this release's bounded repair.

Source inspection only: no probes, benchmarks, tests or edits. This assessment does not reopen accepted correctness review.
effects: None on deciding code, native payload, semantic source, model or formal runtime.
